sections.title: Bone Counts (Important!)
points: A normal adult human being has 206 bones.
A newborn baby has more: between 300 to 305 bones.
Why? Babies are born with many cartilages that later join/fuse together as they grow.
Ossification: The process where cartilages turn into hard bones.

sections.title: What do the bones protect?
points: Skull: Protects the Brain, Eyes, and Middle/Inner ears.
Pelvic Girdle (Hip): Protects the bladder and Reproductive organs (Uterus in women).

sections.title: Living Tissue Facts
points: Bones are NOT dead; they have blood supply and nerves.
The Bone Marrow acts as a factory for making blood cells.
Bones store Calcium and Phosphorus to keep the body strong.

sections.text: The Femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the body! It must support your whole weight when you stand.

cards.mnemonic: Babies are 'Bonus' bones! They fuse as they grow.

cards.fact: The 80 bones in the center of your body (Skull, Spine, Ribs).
cards.mnemonic: Think of an Axle on a bicycle wheel—it's right in the center!
